description: The admitted star's own Gaia source survives both gates and is no other record's.
No catalogue proposes a Gaia source for the admitted star.
The admitted star's Gaia source is a spine record's, so the star ships unbound.
Every Gaia candidate of the admitted star failed a binding gate.
The admitted star's candidates all failed a gate, and SIMBAD's witness under its TYC rescued one.
Two admitted stars reach the same Gaia source, so neither takes it.
A CNS5 nearby-star census row the spine lacks is admitted.
An IV/25 Tycho-2 star with an HD below 100,000 that AT-HYG never linked is admitted.
An IV/25 Tycho-2 star with an HD of 100,000 or more, outside AT-HYG's subset, is admitted.
An I/239 Hipparcos star with no IV/25 entry is admitted.
A Gaia DR3 source at or brighter than the V floor that no primaries record binds is admitted.
An AT-HYG spine row becomes a manifest row on the merge decision it records.
One Gaia source survives both binding gates with no passing rival, and the record binds to it.
Another spine row derives the same Gaia source, so both are withheld and queued for review.
The binding winner has a runner-up that also passed both gates; precedence chose it and the row is queued for review.
A binding candidate refused because its Gaia G is more than a magnitude fainter than the record's printed V.
A binding candidate refused because SIMBAD gives that Gaia source to a different component of the record's system.
No Gaia source survives the binding gates; the record ships unbound.
Every candidate failed a gate, and SIMBAD files the record's own TYC under the one the sibling gate refused, so that one binds.
A binding candidate that passed both gates but lost to a higher-ranked one.
The Sun takes no Gaia binding.
Every designation the primaries give this star already names another record, so it is ledgered onto that record instead of admitted.
A committed review disposition confirms the derived Gaia source.
A committed review disposition leaves the record unbound.
A committed review disposition binds a Gaia source other than the derived one, on its stated evidence.
Review found the spine row duplicates another spine row; it folds onto that row and its SID merges into the survivor's.
No primary publishes this Flamsteed number for the star, so it leaves the record.
No HD primary publishes this HD number for the star, so it leaves the record.
The classic-ID overlay adds a designation the spine row lacked.
The overlay names a further value for a field, carried as an alias the record answers to.
The overlay names a further value for a single-valued field; it is dropped.
The overlay's further value belongs to a companion drawn as its own star, so it is left to that star.
The overlay and the spine disagree on a designation, and the overlay's value is taken.
A curated override keeps the spine's designation over the overlay's.
A curated override sets the designation.
The overlay's designation already names another record, so it is not added.
An earlier row of this build already minted the record this row names.
The row's Gaia source names no record, but its own HIP names one other than the anchor, which is the component.
The row's own Gaia source or HIP names a record already in the catalogue, which is the component.
A same-as edge bridges the row's synthetic key to a Gaia source already in the catalogue, whose record is the component.
The row's ids resolve to its anchor's record, which the naming authority already letters as this component, so that record is the component.
Projected at the anchor's distance, the pair is wider than the 1 pc tidal limit, so it cannot be bound.
A pair's primary promoted as the system anchor's companion has neither its own fit nor a measured offset from the anchor, so it has no position.
The row's component letter is an unresolved aggregate of components that have rows of their own, so it is not one star.
The row has no brightness of its own: no photometry, magnitude difference, WDS magnitude or per-component spectral type, and no renderable orbit.
The row has no Gaia source, no HIP of its own and no composable synthetic key.
The row has neither an independent fit nor a measured separation and position angle off its anchor.
The distance the row states is a parallax a tier above refused, so promoting it would ship the parked record.
The row becomes a new catalogue record.
Promotion decides nothing for the row: a pair's primary that anchors it, or a row in no pair.
A pair's primary resolves to no catalogue record and no escape places it, so its pair runs with no anchor.
An AT-HYG record sitting on the anchor under the anchor's name plus this letter is the component, and moves to the row's position.
